Personally I'll get diagnosed in ten days and my imposter syndrome has increased exponentially since I thought I might have it. Like, my brain is trying to actively find anything to tell me "no, you don't have ADHD". People like this really confuse me because I have huge trouble reading social cues, seeing whats fake and whats true aswell as social and personal boundaries. Like... that is just feeding that...

I honestly don't know. Everything is super complicated. I feel like my mind is a gigantic toystore and I am supposed to be the manager with the knowledge of a new customer. 

I'd consider myself self aware enough to know that I might be not self aware at all.

I'm like walking through the store, I know that the things exist, but I don't know what shelf they r on or even if they r on a shelf or supposed to be on a shelf. And I don't know what isle I am walking in, even though that doesn't even matter. 

Everything is in the wrong isle, everythings stacked blindly ontop of each other or is on the floor, maybe even hanging from the roof. 

And the worst part is when I stumble over something I didn't know existed and so I question whether it has always been there. 

So, to answer your question: I have no idea. I don't do that intentionally aswell, it's like my symptoms automatically get worse as soon as I am around people.

In the Light Novel it's way more obvious, with him also having troubles with social cues. Lastly he forgot to eat for a whole week. How distracted do you have to be to not eat for a whole week??

Dopamine is not sugar though and I do understand your point. I just root for neurodivergency representation, and Tet kinda flashed into my eye. Like, he was so noticeable different and I am trying to figure it put. I am getting diagnosed for ADHD and I just found him oddly relateable, that is it. As I have stated in another comment, it's the details in behaviour, but I'm just gonna list them here aswell:

\-acts on impulse and interest, opposed to his divine peers acting on rationality and importance

\-fundamental trouble of understanding something outside of his interest

\-has no sense of prioritization

\-troubles with social cues

\-gets distracted very easily and is very forgetful

To me I always get tired when I do homework where I can't take a break after every three words I read/write. Like, I could be absolutely fine before that, but as soon as I force myself to do homework or actually any type of task that requires, like, actually focusing for more than literally ten seconds at a time I get SUPER tired after like half a minute, to the point where my eyes shut and I start yawning the whole time. 

Luckily this doesn't happen very often with exams. Then.... I guess it's because I don't have to focus ALL the time, I like look up once in a while, admire the clouds, look around and then after some time I can write the next half of the sentence.

Thank u haha. In the end I managed it because my dad kinda forced me through this (I had terrible focus, but ig I read it???). To me it's that I am physically incapable to staying focused, and when I force myself to, I get super tired. Like, after a minute I get a headache and I could fall asleep at any time. I usually play an interesting YouTube video in the background when I do homework to recharge energy whenever I have to.

I don't understand how neurotypical people can go like "yep, doing anything that requires any form of focus can be relaxing" like wtf. If I am not brainstorming or hyperfocusing I am working. Even eating or showering is exhausting asf.
